thread:
Jamie K: heads up — since the continuous-batcher tweak rolled at 03:00 UTC we see a 35% p95 latency bump on small requests (seq <= 64). grafana: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/bs/continuous-batcher?panel=latency :eyes:
Priya S: link + timeline? is it correlated with kernel selector flip or queue policy change?
Jamie K: timeline: 02:58 heuristic config pushed, 03:00 canary, 03:12 global roll. spike starts ~03:05, p50 ~9ms -> 18ms, p95 ~42ms -> 56ms, throughput flat.
Alex R: can you paste a sample request shape and a kernel decision log? suspect fallback to small-kernel due to join-window split.
Jamie K: sample shapes: many small single-turn prompts (tokens 8-30). pasted kernel log snippet:
```
2026-07-14T03:06:11Z kernel_select: batch_id=2378 shape=[1,8] prefer="large" fallback="small" reason="join_split_detected"
2026-07-14T03:06:11Z kernel_select: batch_id=2379 shape=[1,26] prefer="large" fallback="small" reason="timeout_budget"
```
Alex R: hmm 'join_split_detected' — the join-window heuristic is splitting microbatches to meet token budget, but that causes more small-kernel invocations. small-kernel has worse tail under high interleaving.
Nora L: also saw increased KV cache eviction churn around same time, eviction rate +48%. logs:
```
kvcache: evictions=482 -> 714 window=5m
kvcache: avg_lookup_ms=0.9 -> 1.8
```
Nora L: eviction + cache misses could amplify small-kernel penalty because more prefix warmups.
Devon M: quick experiment idea: reduce join-window aggressiveness and bump token_budget_target from 256->192 for small shapes. we have a flag `batcher.join_bias` and `batcher.token_target`.
Devon M: patch to try (will only affect canary):
```
# canary config
batcher.join_bias: 0.6 -> 0.4
batcher.token_target.small: 256 -> 192
```
Jamie K: running a repro harness now: `./tools/loadtest --shape=small --rps=1200 --duration=15m --trace`
infra-bot: deploy(canary): batcher-config(sha:ab3f7) -> canary namespace. triggered by Devon M.
Jamie K: repro run results (canary): p95 dropped back to ~44ms (from 56ms), p99 still high ~120ms but lower than 145ms at peak. KV evictions down ~20%. attaching minimal perf dump: https://perf.redwood/dumps/2069998888.
Priya S: good signal. Alex, can you look at kernel scheduler trace? especially cross-batch interleaving counts and prefetch stalls.
Alex R: looked — prefetch threads were starved when join-splits produced many tiny batches. scheduler shows increased context switching and warmup windows. My theory: join-window split increases atomicity of prefix fetches and prevents effective KV sharing across microbatches, causing duplicated prefetch and more small-kernel hot-starts.
Alex R: short-term mitigation: revert join_bias -> 0.6 on global and keep token_target=192 on canary, add a microbatch coalescing threshold to avoid splitting batches <8 tokens.
Devon M: I'm +1 to revert join_bias globally if metrics hold for 10m on canary. I'll create a rollout plan.
Jamie K: filing an incident doc and follow-ups: run long-run perf tests with synthetic mix (small/medium/long) and add a unit test that asserts kernel-selection ratio doesn't exceed baseline for small shapes.
ops-bot: incident opened #INC-2026-442: continuous-batcher join-window regression. assigned: Jamie K, Alex R, Devon M.
Priya S: feels like we need a regression test in CI that reproduces KV-cache churn too. adding ticket to backlog. :memo:
Jamie K: ok rolling global revert in 5m if canary stays green. will post results. :thumbsup:
Jamie K: UPDATE 03:45 UTC — revert applied. p95 back within 3% of baseline, p99 down 12%. Keeping token_target=192 for now while we iterate on better coalescing heuristics.
Nora L: leaving traces and KV histograms in the incident doc. next: simulate mixed-rps spikes to ensure no hidden throughput regressions.
Alex R: follow-up action items: (1) implement microbatch coalesce threshold (2) adjust prefetch scheduling to dedupe prefix fetches across imminent splits (3) add CI perf test that asserts kernel choice distribution.
Jamie K: thanks all. good catch. we'll track in the incident and schedule a postmortem if the revert had any side effects. :white_check_mark:
